title: RFID Ammo Can Tag — Military Ammunition Container ID
summary: RFID ammo can tags put a MIL-STD-129R / MIL-STD-1168D DODIC + LOT identifier on PA70 / M2A1 / PA108 ammo cans, readable at 3-5 m. The GIAI-96 payload adds UN hazard class / division, compatibility group and NEW for DOT 49 CFR §173.62 Class 1 Explosives transport. MIL-STD-810H-qualified on-metal hardware survives -40 °C to +85 °C, and DoD 5160.65-M surveillance cycles run as automated EPCIS events.
keywords: MIL-STD-129R + MIL-STD-1168D DODIC / NALC / LOT marking
heroPoints: MIL-STD-129R / MIL-STD-130N IUID-aligned per-container identifier on every PA70 / PA108 / PA120 / M2A1 / M2A2 / M19A1 ammo can and 40 mm / 155 mm pallet — encodes DODIC + NALC + LOT + PA-INTERIM + DoDAAC + hazard-class label per MIL-STD-129R §5 + MIL-STD-1168D + UN Recommendations on Transport of Dangerous Goods.

Dock-door portal + handheld UHF architecture — wall-to-wall inventory of a 50,000-container ASP / MMAC / MCAAP depot via walk-by / drive-by reads; DoD 5160.65-M ammunition surveillance cycles and MIL-STD-129R §5.5 DODIC / lot reconciliation run as automated EPCIS events instead of paper issue slips.

MIL-STD-810H-qualified, DOT 49 CFR §173.62-aware hardware — on-metal UHF survives -40 °C to +85 °C, MIL-STD-810H Methods 501 / 502 / 507 / 509 / 510 / 514 / 516 shock / vibration / sand / dust / salt-fog; Class 1 Div 2 / ATEX Zone 22 portal stack supported; no pyrotechnic / propellant-incompatibility risk when encoded in a secured cell off the explosive line.
imageAlt: RFID ammo can tag on an M2A1 / PA108 military ammunition container for MIL-STD-129R / MIL-STD-1168D DODIC + NALC + LOT marking, DOT 49 CFR §173.62 Class 1 Explosives transport, ITAR USML Category III export, ATF 27 CFR Part 555 commerce in explosives and DoD 5160.65-M ammunition surveillance

brief.label: Chip options
brief.text: {chip:impinj-monza-r6-p:name} for baseline PA70 / M2A1 / M2A2 / M19A1 / PA108 / PA120 containers; {chip:impinj-m750:name} / M770 / M775 for 40 mm crate / 155 mm pallet long-range yard portal reads; {chip:nxp-ucode-9:name} / 9xe for extended user-memory carrying DODIC + NALC + LOT + DoDAAC + hazard-class + UN hazard ID on-tag for disconnected-mode reads at remote ammunition supply points (ASPs); {chip:alien-higgs-9:name} for densely-stacked igloo-to-pallet reads. NTAG424 DNA (13.56 MHz HF) with SUN CMAC AES-128 per-tap signature per NXP AN12196 for ITAR-controlled USML Category III lots, federal law-enforcement evidence ammunition, ATF 27 CFR Part 555 explosive-materials transfers and NATO STANAG 2493 Tier-1 programmes where per-container cryptographic signing is required.

brief.label: Frequency / air interface
brief.text: 860-960 MHz UHF Gen2v2 per EPCglobal Class 1 Gen 2 v2.1 + ISO/IEC 18000-63:2015 for yard portal, dock-door, igloo and handheld reads; 13.56 MHz HF per ISO/IEC 14443-3 Type A + NFC Forum Type 4 Tag Operation v3.0 for NTAG424 DNA per-container forensic tap; readers with ATEX Zone 21 / 22 + IECEx + UL / CSA Class I Div 2 / Class II Div 1-2 ratings for ammunition / propellant-dust-adjacent operations per NFPA 484 + NFPA 495; MIL-STD-461G / RS103 EMC profile for deployed reader stacks; FCC Part 15 / ETSI EN 302 208 / IC RSS-247 spectrum compliance.

brief.label: Asset identifier scheme
brief.text: MIL-STD-129R §5 military shipping label + MIL-STD-1168D DODIC / NALC / LOT assignment encoded as a GS1 GIAI-96 per GS1 Tag Data Standard 2.0 §7.1 carrying the full DODIC (4-character munition code) + NALC (2-character interim) + LOT serial + DoDAAC consignee / consignor + UN hazard class / division (1.1 / 1.2 / 1.3 / 1.4 / 1.5 / 1.6) + compatibility group (A-S) per DOT 49 CFR §173.52 + NEW (Net Explosive Weight) per 49 CFR §172.202 + hazard-division placard (ORM-D for small-arms, Class 1.4S) + ATF 27 CFR §555.109 marking of explosive materials + ITAR USML Category III export control flag + manufacturer CAGE code + date of pack per DoD 5160.65-M. Container events publish as EPCIS 2.0 ObjectEvents with bizStep=shipping / receiving / storing / issuing / demilitarizing and disposition keyed to DoD 5160.65-M surveillance state (serviceable / unserviceable-reparable / unserviceable-condemned).

brief.label: Form-factor SKUs (6)
brief.text: (1) PA70 / M2A1 .50-cal can (100 × 50 mm on-metal tag screwed / riveted into spare stencil panel on lid or sidewall, Monza R6-P + UCODE 9); (2) PA108 / M2A2 / M19A1 larger can (100 × 50 mm + reinforced epoxy potted per MIL-DTL-24203 ammunition-box paint-system compatibility); (3) PA120 / PA125 modern fiber-reinforced plastic can (anti-metal not required — flexible UHF inlay bonded to lid); (4) 40 mm / 25 mm / 20 mm wooden crate / PA116 / PA117 (20 × 10 mm on-wood staple-mount inlay + QR-code fallback per MIL-STD-129R §5.8); (5) 155 mm / 105 mm projectile pallet (80 × 40 mm long-range M775 for 5-8 m portal read on palletized unitized loads per MIL-STD-1660); (6) SAAMI sporting-arms case / commercial cardboard outer (flexible UHF 50 × 25 mm on cardboard + adhesive backing; SAAMI Z299.1-5-aware encoding for commercial distribution including ATF 27 CFR §478.121 / NICS records).

brief.label: Environmental & hazardous-area rating
brief.text: IP67 / IP68; ATEX / IECEx Zone 21 / 22 dust-rated readers + tags for propellant-dust / small-arms-primer-dust operations; UL / CSA Class I Div 2 + Class II Div 1-2 for propellant / pyrotechnic atmospheres per NFPA 495 / NFPA 400; MIL-HDBK-1013 physical security of sensitive conventional arms; DoD 4145.26-M contractor's safety manual for ammunition / explosives compatibility verified per DESR 6055.09 Edition 1; NFPA 70 Art. 500 hazardous-classified-location wiring at the ASP portal; no intrinsic-safety rating needed on the passive RFID tag itself (zero active emissions).

sections.title: Why paper DD Form 1348 / 1387-2 + stencil marking fails MIL-STD-129R + ATF + DOT audit
bullets: MIL-STD-129R §5 military shipping label + MIL-STD-1168D DODIC / NALC / LOT marking requirements are routinely executed via stencil, paint-pen and paper DD Form 1348 / 1387-2. ASP / MMAC / MCAAP depots with 50,000+ containers cannot reconcile depot-paper state to SAAS-MOD / TAMIS-R / GCSS-Army / MHP in real time, producing surveillance-cycle gaps the DCSA ammunition-safety inspector regularly cites.

DoD 5160.65-M single-manager-for-conventional-ammunition surveillance windows (quarterly / semi-annual / annual dependent on family) are tracked on paper ammunition-condition-code cards. Out-of-cycle lots slip to unserviceable-reparable before the condition-code review — a preventable-loss finding under DESR 6055.09.

DOT 49 CFR §173.62 Class 1 Explosives + §172.202 NEW + §173.52 compatibility-group marking depends on stencil legibility in salt-fog / sand / desert storage. Weathered stencils drive carrier-refusal events, placard mismatches and HMIS citations during DOT roadside inspection.

ATF 27 CFR Part 555 Commerce in Explosives (§555.109 marking, §555.127 records of transactions) and ATF Explosives Tracing Center requests turn into multi-hour paper-pull exercises at law-enforcement bomb-squad evidence stores, explosives distributors and SAAMI-aligned manufacturers.

ITAR 22 CFR 120-130 USML Category III export-controlled lots require tight custody documentation. Paper chain-of-custody during contractor-to-DoD-to-coalition transfers cannot defend an ITAR audit or meet NATO STANAG 2493 marking / STANAG 4439 insensitive-munitions documentation.

MIL-STD-810H-qualified hardware survives CARC-paint compatibility, -40 °C to +85 °C, 96 h salt-fog, sand/dust, shock, vibration including Method 514 vehicle-transport + Annex C ballistic-transport profile. ATEX Zone 22 + Class II Div 1-2 portal stack handles propellant-dust environments. Tag encoding occurs in a bonded facility off the explosive line per DoD 4145.26-M.

Wiring into SAAS-MOD / TAMIS-R / GCSS-Army / MHP / LIW / OIS-MC / CAS / ROLMS-I + DoD IUID Registry via PIEE / iRAPT. Feeds cover ATF eForm 6 + Explosives Tracing Center + FBI WMDD / HAZMAT, SAAMI-aligned manufacturer ERPs, DOT HMIS + carrier HazMat feeds, ITAR DTrade + CHIEF / ACE customs, and NATO AASTP-1 / STANAG 2493 export for coalition operations.

faq.question: Is the tag compatible with ammunition / propellant-adjacent storage and encoding?
faq.answer: Yes. The tag is passive (no battery, no emissions) and encoded in a bonded facility off the explosive line per DoD 4145.26-M contractor's safety manual and DESR 6055.09 DoD explosives-safety standards. The reader stack for propellant-dust atmospheres uses ATEX / IECEx Zone 21 / 22 + UL / CSA Class I Div 2 / Class II Div 1-2 ratings per NFPA 495 / NFPA 400 / NFPA 484. Because the passive tag emits no RF energy itself, it poses no hazardous-materials compatibility risk to the contained Class 1 munitions.

faq.question: How does the programme encode MIL-STD-129R + MIL-STD-1168D DODIC / NALC / LOT?
faq.answer: The full MIL-STD-129R §5 military shipping label vector is encoded in a GS1 GIAI-96 carrier per GS1 TDS 2.0 §7.1. That vector spans DODIC (4-character munition code), NALC (2-character interim), LOT serial, DoDAAC consignor / consignee, UN hazard class / division (1.1-1.6), compatibility group (A-S) per DOT 49 CFR §173.52, NEW per §172.202, manufacturer CAGE, and date of pack per DoD 5160.65-M. EPCIS 2.0 events feed SAAS-MOD / TAMIS-R / GCSS-Army / MHP / OIS-MC / CAS / ROLMS-I and the DoD IUID Registry via PIEE / iRAPT.

faq.question: Does it handle ATF 27 CFR Part 555 explosive-materials and ITAR export-controlled lots?
faq.answer: Yes. The tag auto-generates the ATF 27 CFR §555.127 records of transactions and §555.109 marking verification for every transfer; the export feed pushes to ATF eForm 6 / Explosives Tracing Center on demand. ITAR 22 CFR 120-130 USML Category III lots use the NTAG424 DNA SUN CMAC AES-128 variant for per-scan cryptographic signing (per NXP AN12196), and the key-management pack supports ITAR registration audits, DCSA physical-security inspection, and NATO STANAG 2493 / STANAG 4439 coalition-transfer documentation.

faq.question: Will the tag survive MIL-STD-810H transport and CARC-paint recoating?
faq.answer: Yes. The housing is polycarbonate / polyurethane / ABS overmold with MIL-DTL-24203 CARC-paint-compatible surface; the tag passes MIL-STD-810H Method 501 / 502 (-40 °C to +85 °C), Method 514 vibration including Procedure I vehicle-transport + Annex C ballistic-transport profile, Method 516 shock (40g / 11 ms half-sine), Method 509 salt fog (96 h), Method 510 sand/dust, Method 507 humidity (10 cycles); and MIL-STD-810H Method 520 combined environments. ASTM B117 1,000 h for naval storage is validated. Read performance is preserved after CARC recoating.
